Direct adoption reached first token sooner in all three fixed low-logging pairs versus matched project ARC demand restoration. Adoption-minus-demand intended-release TTFT deltas were -28.967, -29.013, -29.062 ms. Every correctness gate passed and all per-seed paired output token lists and ordered prompt-key digests matched across 264 requests. This is a small privileged-target diagnostic; it does not establish significance, deployable prediction, broad repeatability or no worse background behavior. No workload retuning, additional arm, model build or implementation repair ran.

| Seed | Arm order | Demand release→token ms | Adopt release→token ms | Delta ms | Submit-TTFT delta ms |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1103 | demand→adopt | 70.864 | 41.897 | -28.967 | -28.232 |
| 2207 | adopt→demand | 71.285 | 42.273 | -29.013 | -29.191 |
| 3301 | demand→adopt | 71.350 | 42.288 | -29.062 | -29.000 |

All times include client-visible overhead. Release lateness is included in release→token, with actual-submit TTFT separate. Three seeds reuse one workload and are not independent deployment samples. Observed demand spread was 70.864–71.350 ms and adoption 41.897–42.288 ms; these combine order/system variation and seed effects, not an isolated noise estimate. No p95 or confidence interval is claimed.

| Seed | Background TTFT delta ms | Mean-ITL delta ms | Elapsed delta ms | Tokens/s delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1103 | 3.853 | 0.027 | 17.630 | -0.140 |
| 2207 | 0.185 | 0.015 | 7.868 | -0.062 |
| 3301 | -1.014 | 0.015 | 6.755 | -0.053 |

Background generated 512 tokens; mean ITL divides first-to-last receipt span by511 intervals, and throughput divides512 by actual submit-to-completion seconds. Decode spanned resume in all six arms, with request overlap 2218.366–2245.550 ms. The background deltas are observations, not a no-harm equivalence test. Full absolute denominators and stream timestamps remain in measurements/raw. All six timing arms completed 1,584 requests; readiness adds 264. There were zero request failures or preemptions.

| Arm | Submit TTFT ms | Release lateness ms | BG TTFT ms | BG mean ITL ms | BG elapsed ms | BG tokens/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| p1-demand | 69.652 | 1.211 | 18.263 | 15.674 | 8027.910 | 63.777 |
| p1-adopt | 41.420 | 0.476 | 22.116 | 15.701 | 8045.540 | 63.638 |
| p2-adopt | 40.951 | 1.322 | 20.456 | 15.711 | 8048.771 | 63.612 |
| p2-demand | 70.141 | 1.144 | 20.271 | 15.696 | 8040.903 | 63.674 |
| p3-demand | 70.097 | 1.253 | 20.802 | 15.700 | 8043.804 | 63.651 |
| p3-adopt | 41.097 | 1.191 | 19.788 | 15.716 | 8050.560 | 63.598 |

Each fresh server used the unchanged exact 2048-token Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct prefix, BF16/TP1/block16,640 GPU blocks/280MiB pool,448MiB DRAM,128 staging blocks,750ms correct-target lead, native ARC threshold2, request_order, soft retention off, owned_reclaimable, deterministic eager/batch-invariant generation and maxlen8192. Identical 256 cold-source qualification requests with GPU-only reset and 6 fixed pressure prompts preceded each gap. Background512 output tokens released100ms before resume 128. Both arms published the same pending correct-target hint at wait origin; release never awaited RPC acknowledgment. Sole generic config difference was wait_hint_diagnostic_no_dispatch; native_adoption=true in both. This baseline is project ARC with matched hint bookkeeping, not vanilla upstream ARC.

At hint origin every arm proved 128 exact DRAM-ready blocks and zero usable GPU prefix blocks. Adoption performed a real 56MiB H2D transfer with successful TP1 completion before publication. It reused exactly the 128 staged physical IDs under native hash/group/refcount checks, then the actual worker consumed those IDs with 2048 computed tokens,129 initial blocks and 14 locally executed suffix prompt tokens. Adoption had zero target demand H2D and numeric zero GPU splice bytes. Demand performed real 56MiB H2D after resume, with successful completion before worker use and the exact demand destination IDs/keys consumed. Its splice counter is null because no splice state exists: no advance staging/publication or splice acknowledgment was reported; null is not presented as measured zero. Readiness alone additionally read the actual small CUDA block table and matched all IDs. Full KV tensors were not independently bitwise dumped; real generated outputs and ordered prompt keys matched per seed. No new GPU cancellation/failure injection or layout coverage was added.

Adoption real H2D completion was -747.013–-746.712 ms relative to release; stage-ready -745.585–-745.235 ms; native publication 9.572–9.889 ms; allocator adoption 9.928–10.230 ms; worker execute entry 10.092–10.392 ms; worker attention preparation 10.592–11.074 ms. Demand transfer completion was 17.464–19.163 ms and attention preparation 39.514–40.028 ms. Scheduler adoption is not worker/device ready. Worker timestamps are host boundaries, not kernel-completion timestamps. The latency difference includes CPU/scheduling/transfer round trips; no overlapping DMA time is added to runner time.

Each arm transferred 7,516,192,768 H2D bytes across prep+gap and 58,720,256 D2H bytes during prep. Gap H2D was 56MiB in both and gap D2H zero. This confirms no observed competing gap store admissions; it does not erase prefetch CPU/source-protection asymmetry. Actual speculative source refs/protection and advance 128-block reservation exist only with dispatch. Target allocation failures were zero; sampled 640-block pool accounting was consistent. Adoption staging peaked at 56MiB and reservation byte-time was 42.491, 42.474, 42.471 MiB·s. Native handoff used one prefix copy; sampled referenced-block peaks were 147, 147, 147, 147, 147, 147. These are pool occupancy observations, not reduced preallocated VRAM. No capacity gain was measured.

Lighter logging was active identically: mandatory native transfer events/completion metadata retained; rich perstep lookup, CPU-cache/physical mapping snapshots and preservation serialization disabled; TorchDispatch query capture and perstep CUDA memory_stats removed. Numeric scheduler accounting, small symmetric worker host block-table mirror, one-time ordered-key capture/digest, compact 264 terminal receipts and target transition receipts remain. Timed arms add no CUDA synchronization; readiness's tiny table read is excluded. Actual logs were 315,956–352,105 bytes versus 79,347,630–79,644,596 bytes previously, with zero rich preservation events in every new arm. Native required staging/publication metadata still differs by branch; observation overhead is reduced, not eliminated. Removed rich checks are not claimed as rerun. logging-change.json records exact hooks/config evidence. CPU hook accounting/terminal-drain checks passed 3 cases without CUDA initialization; unchanged production code retains prior CPU and GPU validation. The one initial demand analysis assertion concerned null-counter semantics only and was corrected without rerun or hook change; its failure is preserved.

The consistent latency edge is enough to consider a separately authorized next capacity test, but this screen does not establish background neutrality or capacity improvement. Advance reservations could compete with other demand; capacity/interference must be measured separately. No next experiment was executed. Review applied research-review directly; no independent reviewer under the no-child execution brief.

Source/runtime bytes are unchanged from the parent-integrated implementation. Baseline/current pins, tracked status and recovered-source/wheel provenance are in frozen.json/audit.json and ../evidence/implementation-pins.json. This is not exact historical runtime-tree recovery. No source patch, commit, push, dependency download or build was needed. Task-local hooks/tools are exportable in reproduction-tools.tar.gz with verified member hashes; existing full/delta/runtime patches are included. REPRODUCE.md gives commands.

Seven model lifecycles used approximately 483.0 seconds (8.1 minutes) of driver wall time including startup, qualification, generation, shutdown and compression; GPU busy time was not measured. 1,848 requests generated19,152 tokens and locally executed1,953,511 prompt tokens. Fresh enforcing native-Windows quiet custody covered all arms; no other owner was interrupted. Raw/log payloads remain lossless gzip with round-trip hashes. Storage-steward bounded inventory is storage-handback.json; reusable environment/shared caches/recovery sources and all prior evidence are preserved. Final ownership/restoration/release verification is cleanup.json and CURRENT.md.

Evidence: evidence/measurements.json (all paired deltas, gates, metrics and exactness), measurements.csv, *-detail.json (target/worker/hint receipts), frozen.json, logging-change.json, audit.json; results/*/raw.json.gz, server*.log.gz, compression.json; evidence/*.activity.json (actual mediated descendant receipts). Operational lifecycle cleanup status is only final once cleanup.json exists and reports release.
